title: Session Management
description: Flaws in token entropy, lifecycle management, cookie security scopes, session invalidation, and cross-site request forgery protections.

attacks.name: Session token entropy analysis
attacks.desc: Collecting thousands of sequentially issued session identifiers to statistically calculate bitwise randomness and detect predictable PRNG patterns susceptible to token prediction.
attacks.prevention: Generate session identifiers with a cryptographically secure random generator and test their entropy and length.

attacks.name: Session prediction
attacks.desc: Calculating valid session tokens by identifying predictable inputs such as user ID, creation timestamp, IP address, or weak hashing algorithms used to construct session keys.
attacks.prevention: Use unpredictable opaque session tokens and avoid timestamps, counters, or user IDs as token material.

attacks.name: Session fixation
attacks.desc: Establishing a known session token in a victim's browser prior to authentication that remains bound to the account after the user logs in, granting the attacker persistent access.
attacks.prevention: Create a fresh session ID after login and privilege changes, and invalidate the pre-authentication ID.

attacks.name: Session hijacking
attacks.desc: Acquiring an active user's session identifier through network sniffing, XSS exploitation, logging leaks, or physical access to impersonate the victim without credentials.
attacks.prevention: Use HTTPS, Secure and HttpOnly cookies, narrow cookie scope, and rotate or revoke tokens when compromise is suspected.

attacks.name: Session timeout absence
attacks.desc: Maintaining sessions indefinitely without enforcing idle or absolute timeout thresholds, increasing the exposure window for stolen or abandoned session tokens.
attacks.prevention: Enforce idle and absolute session expiry on the server rather than depending on browser closure.

attacks.name: Session not invalidated on logout
attacks.desc: Removing session cookies from the client browser on logout without destroying the associated session record in the backend server database, allowing replayed tokens to remain functional.
attacks.prevention: Revoke the server-side session and clear its cookie on logout; reject the old token on every endpoint.

attacks.name: Session not invalidated on password change
attacks.desc: Failing to terminate all existing active sessions when a user updates their password, allowing unauthorized actors with compromised sessions to maintain access.

attacks.name: Concurrent session flaws
attacks.desc: Allowing an account to maintain limitless simultaneous active sessions from distinct geographic regions and IP subnets without anomaly detection or single-session enforcement.

attacks.name: Cookie scope / path issues
attacks.desc: Setting overly broad cookie Domain attributes (e.g. Domain=.example.com) or omitting strict Path limits, causing session tokens to be leaked to vulnerable or untrusted subdomains.

attacks.name: CSRF
attacks.desc: Tricking an authenticated victim into submitting an unwanted HTTP request to a target application that blindly trusts the victim's session cookies.

attacks.name: CSRF token missing / predictable
attacks.desc: Omitting cryptographic anti-CSRF tokens in state-changing POST/PUT requests, or utilizing predictable tokens derived from usernames or timestamps.

attacks.name: CSRF token not validated
attacks.desc: Generating anti-CSRF tokens on the server but failing to verify them upon receiving requests, or bypassing verification when the token parameter is completely removed.

attacks.name: SameSite bypass
attacks.desc: Circumventing SameSite cookie protections through top-level navigations, client redirects, subdomain takeover, or exploiting the 2-minute Lax-under-POST window in modern browsers.

attacks.name: Cross-site WebSocket hijacking
attacks.desc: Initiating cross-origin WebSocket handshakes from an attacker's website using the victim's ambient browser cookies to establish two-way communication channels with sensitive backend endpoints.

attacks.name: Session puzzling
attacks.desc: Manipulating multi-step workflows to overwrite critical session variables (such as user role or authentication status) by accessing disparate application endpoints in unexpected order.

attacks.name: Session replay
attacks.desc: Capturing legitimate authenticated HTTP transactions and replaying them against the server to duplicate actions (such as financial transactions) when nonce or timestamp verification is absent.
